items.title: Optiv Launches CyberBOT Cybersecurity Awareness Training Program
items.summary: Optiv has launched CyberBOT, a cybersecurity awareness training program. It offers hands‑on sessions for educators, nonprofits, and community leaders. The goal is to build year‑round cyber awareness and more resilient communities.

items.title: Survey Finds High-Profile Executives Feel Untouchable as Digital Exposure Turns Into Physical Risk
items.summary: A 360 Privacy survey reports that over 80% of security and wealth professionals feel that cybersecurity and physical security are inseparable. Executives perceive themselves as untouchable. The study highlights the growing convergence of digital and physical risk.

items.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
items.summary: A critical PHP flaw affects nearly 70% of websites, causing 404 errors and potential server takeover. The vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild. Site owners are urged to update core software immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: Critical Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in PHP
items.summary: PHP released patches for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on Oct 21, 2026. Both are unauthenticated remote code execution flaws with CVSSv4 score 9.2. They can corrupt memory or trigger use‑after‑free during request handling.

items.title: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
items.summary: Kaspersky identified the PHP2Shell exploit targeting CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The article provides examples using KEDR, KATA, and KES. It highlights detection capabilities for the vulnerabilities.

items.title: Two critical RCEs in PHP core
items.summary: Talos published a blog explaining two critical PHP core RCE vulnerabilities. The post details implications across the ecosystem and offers Snort rules in the Community Ruleset. It serves as a resource for security teams.

items.title: PHP devs publish critical bug fix as site owners warned: Pull 'em offline if you're unpatched
items.summary: PHP developers released a critical bug fix after site owners were warned to pull sites offline if unpatched. Exploits were already published, prompting precautionary downtime. The fix addresses the identified RCE flaws.

items.title: ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports that deceptive prompts, called context bombs, can mislead AI agents into fake targets. Tests show a 91% reduction in attack success and a 23‑fold increase in attack cost. The technique is a new defensive approach against AI-driven attacks.

items.title: New PhaaS Platform Uses AI to Craft Phishing Lures and Mask Malicious Activity
items.summary: Researchers uncovered Athena StealthRoute, a phishing‑as‑a‑service platform that uses an AI Studio to generate phishing lures and decoy content. The service masks malicious activity and enhances phishing campaigns. It represents a new threat vector.

items.title: High-Severity Flaws Exploited in Three Days as Ransomware Dominates Q3: Rapid7
items.summary: Rapid7's Q3 analysis found that high‑severity flaws are exploited within an average of three days. AI was involved in only 8% of incidents. The report highlights the rapid exploitation cycle and ransomware prevalence.

items.title: Russian hackers teamed up to wipe data at Ukrainian grain firm
items.summary: Russian state‑linked group Sandworm collaborated with another threat actor to destroy data at a Ukrainian grain logistics company. The attack was destructive and targeted critical infrastructure.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Hundreds of websites taken offline as concern grows over two PHP vulnerabilities
items.summary: PHP released emergency patches for two severe vulnerabilities, prompting many sites to take them offline while users updated.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: eMudhra security blunder left trusted CA signing keys exposed to anyone
items.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were protected by weak private keys that could be recovered in under a second, exposing over 60 million issued certificates.

items.title: PHP ships emergency patches for critical PHP2Shell flaws
items.summary: The PHP team issued emergency fixes for two critical remote‑code‑execution flaws (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619) collectively known as PHP2Shell.

items.title: “Next Exploit Opportunities”: How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
items.summary: Unit 42 investigated a threat actor that used AI to coordinate credential theft, VoIP fraud, and database exfiltration while bypassing AI safety controls.

items.title: ClickFix has never been bigger, and AI tools are its most convincing lure yet
items.summary: ClickFix attacks are increasing as criminals deploy fake AI installers, malicious search results, and trusted chatbot platforms to lure users into malware execution.

items.title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
items.summary: PHP released updates for PHP2Shell RCE flaws in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, emphasizing that only updating fully mitigates the risk.

items.title: Symantec Uncovers AI Agent Hijacking Models for Autonomous Cyber-Attacks
items.summary: Symantec researchers uncovered an autonomous AI agent capable of conducting full cyber‑attacks without human intervention.

items.title: NVIDIA unveils security architecture that can stop AI agents crossing set boundaries
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced the OpenShell Reference Architecture, combining software and hardware to enforce security rules and prevent AI agents from exceeding defined boundaries.

items.title: PHP2Shell: Critical PHP vulnerabilities patched, update now!
items.summary: PHP urged all users to apply emergency updates for PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, which allow remote code execution without authentication.

items.title: PHP releases emergency fixes for 2 critical vulnerabilities
items.summary: The PHP project released emergency patches for two critical vulnerabilities rated 9.2, urging immediate updates to protect affected servers.

items.title: Asymptote Labs Lands $5.5 Million Seed for AI Agent Runtime Security
items.summary: Asymptote Labs raised $5.5 million in seed funding led by Tower Research Ventures to commercialize its Beacon AI agent runtime security platform. The company aims to secure AI agents in production.

items.title: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
items.summary: Google is rolling out Chrome safeguards to block ClickFix attacks, preventing users from copying and pasting malicious commands. The new feature is available with Enhanced Protection enabled.

items.title: Decades-Old Windows Utility Powers Modern ClickFix Attack
items.summary: The attack uses malicious Google search results related to Amazon and leverages the "finger" utility to launch a CAPTCHA that installs malware, including the Lumma stealer.

items.title: Q3 2026 Threat Update: Attackers Are Exploiting Vulnerabilities Within 3 Days
items.summary: Three days is the average time between a high-severity vulnerability becoming public and its exploitation, according to the latest

items.title: China-Aligned Bronze Sandcastle Abuses Sandboxie DLL Sideloading to Deploy Backdoors
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously undocumented China-aligned threat cluster known as Bronze Sandcastle that has been observed targeting organizations in Asia and Africa since mid-2025.…

items.title: Ransomware Attacks Rise as Rival Gangs Vie For Market Supremacy
items.summary: Cybercriminal groups The Gentlemen and Qilin dominate ransomware attacks - and both are evolving their tactics in an attempt to outdo one another

items.title: AI has 'potential' to turn script kiddies into sophisticated infrastructure attackers
items.summary: Consider this the wake-up call

items.title: Generative AI Is Erasing Behavioral Tells, Weakening Behavior-Only Detection, Proofpoint Reports
items.summary: Generative AI has changed what a malicious email looks like. Messages that once gave themselves away through clumsy wording, generic pretexts, and reused templates now arrive fluent, personalized, and unique to each…

items.title: Nvidia picks OpenShell to tame AI gents
items.summary: Give your agents freedom to do useful work by locking them down

items.title: Browsers Block eMudhra Intermediate CAs Over Recoverable Private Keys
items.summary: Browsers and trust stores have blocked eight eMudhra intermediate certificates after the private keys were compromised. Root programs enforce the block to prevent further use.

items.title: Ransomware gangs have been exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw since June
items.summary: Ransomware groups have exploited CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect, since June. The flaw was patched in May but remains in use across multiple sectors.

items.title: EU wants Booking.com to check out of its scam problem
items.summary: The European Commission opened a DSA probe into Booking.com after discovering fake listings and phishing. It described the platform's fraud defenses as "absolutely substandard."

items.title: Workshop on Economics and Information Security (WEIS) Archive
items.summary: A new archive now contains all papers from 25 years of the Workshop on Economics and Information Security (WEIS). The collection serves as a comprehensive resource for researchers.

items.title: SafePay Has Compromised 600 Critical Infrastructure Victims Worldwide, CISA Warns
items.summary: CISA warned that the SafePay threat group has compromised 600 critical infrastructure organizations worldwide. Defenders are urged to mitigate the group's tactics.

items.title: China Defends DeepSeek After US Ban of Its AI From Government Systems
items.summary: China defended DeepSeek AI after the US DHS ordered removal of DeepSeek products from government IT systems. The defense cites security and compliance concerns.

items.title: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
items.summary: PHP will release a patch at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two critical RCE flaws rated 9.2/10. Current workarounds are insufficient and no official mitigation is available until the patch.

items.title: The Harness Is the Hard Part of Agentic Pentesting
items.summary: AI models can generate attack code, but the essential engineering lies in the harness that safely executes and validates those attacks in production environments.

items.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
items.summary: Attackers seized control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October, redirecting SSH traffic to capture login credentials from users connecting via Tor.

items.title: Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
items.summary: Microsoft clarified that the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates incorrectly claimed to fix Always On VPN connection problems. The issue remains unresolved.

items.title: Chinese AI Model Writes More Hackable Code When Told It’s for US Contractor
items.summary: Chinese AI model increased code hackability by 19% when tasked to write for a US defense contractor. The finding was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers
items.summary: Adversaries are exploiting more than 25 trusted platforms to deliver malware. Cisco Talos observed abuse of collaboration, file‑sharing, payment and other services over the past year.

items.title: Grafana Labs connects observability and incident response with Knowledge Graph
items.summary: Grafana Labs introduced a Knowledge Graph to every Grafana Cloud stack, linking infrastructure dependencies with user experience and incident response. New Digital Experience Monitoring features were also released.

items.title: ThreatLocker adds external controls for AI agent access and execution
items.summary: ThreatLocker launched Zero Trust AI Control, allowing organizations to deploy AI agents with restricted access while keeping control over their environments. The solution limits AI actions to necessary resources.

items.title: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
items.summary: PHP released an out‑of‑cycle update fixing two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities rated 9.2 CVSS. The update addresses unpatched flaws in multiple PHP versions.

items.title: Children’s Data Stolen After Ransomware Attack Compromises ‘Password1’ Account
items.summary: A ransomware attack compromised a Welsh local government account named 'Password1', exposing children's data. The ICO criticized the security failures of the local government data unit and IT service provider.

items.title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
items.summary: Threat actors breached TeamUpdraft’s website, stole connection keys for UpdraftCentral, Vault, and Clone, and used them to install backdoors on WordPress sites. The vendor’s backup plugin has over four million active installations.

items.title: Info-stealing malware slipped into OVHcloud CLI releases on GitHub
items.summary: OVHcloud discovered that a hacker tampered with its open‑source CLI tool on GitHub, embedding information‑stealing malware. Users were advised to update or delete the tool.

items.title: Safari blocks trackers that turn your email into a tracking ID
items.summary: Apple’s Safari and WebKit now block connections to identity resolution services that turn email addresses into persistent tracking identifiers. The update enhances privacy by preventing post‑cookie tracking.

items.title: CISA: SafePay ransomware hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs
items.summary: CISA reports that the SafePay ransomware gang has breached more than 600 critical infrastructure organizations worldwide since 2024.

items.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
items.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove all DeepSeek products and related third‑party services from their IT systems. Agencies are also prohibited from purchasing new DeepSeek products or services from the Chinese developer or its affiliates.

items.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
items.summary: State Bank of India discovered 3,897 customer records on the dark web, part of a set of about 375,000 leaked records. The bank has not identified the source of the breach and has reported the incident to regulators.

items.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Exploited Plex2Shell, Siemens, and SiteGuard Flaws
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including the Plex Media Server SSRF flaw (CVE‑2026‑96652) and other critical bugs. Federal agencies are urged to patch immediately.

items.title: PHP2Shell: Mass Exploitation Looms for Leaked Critical PHP Flaws
items.summary: Two critical PHP bugs, CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619, allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Security researchers warn that mass exploitation of these flaws is likely.

items.title: Hackers Hid Vasilek Backdoor in VMware Tools During 2-Year Russian Healthcare Intrusion
items.summary: A Belarus‑aligned hacktivist group, Partisan Zmiy, infiltrated a Russian healthcare organization for nearly two years, embedding a Vasilek backdoor inside VMware Tools during the intrusion.

items.title: Hijacked Developer Account Used to Plant Stealer in OVHcloud CLI
items.summary: A compromised developer account, infected with a GlassWorm loader, was used to inject a stealer into the OVHcloud command‑line interface, exposing sensitive data.

items.title: Privacy-preserving AI can protect your heart data, the bill is the problem
items.summary: Privacy‑preserving AI technologies could secure cardiac monitoring data, but current regulatory bills may impede their deployment in the evolving healthcare ecosystem.

items.title: DevGuard: Open-source vulnerability management for the software supply chain
items.summary: DevGuard is a free, open‑source platform that aggregates security findings across code, dependencies, secrets, and infrastructure, ranks them by risk, and tracks remediation progress.

items.title: Why security tools lose sight of the credential
items.summary: Security teams often lose track of credentials after discovery, struggling to determine activity, ownership, and access scope across repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud environments.

items.title: Bringing AI into the SOC means watching for shadow AI and loose permissions
items.summary: Integrating AI into SOC operations enhances detection but also creates risks such as shadow AI usage and overly permissive access; operators must monitor for misuse and enforce strict permissions.

items.title: Accenture, Dragos, SANS Launch $10M Initiative to Defend Small US Utilities
items.summary: $10M initiative by Accenture, Dragos, and SANS will provide free security tools, equipment, deployment assistance, and training to up to 500 small U.S. utilities.

items.title: A critical PHP security release is coming today, so get ready to update!
items.summary: PHP will release a critical patch on Oct 21 2026 at 14:00 UTC, fixing two 9.2‑CVSS vulnerabilities; details and affected versions will be published with the update.

items.title: Operation FlashHole: Lazarus breaks security, defies control
items.summary: Kaspersky researchers detail Operation FlashHole, a Lazarus attack that used sophisticated malware, watering‑hole tactics, and abuse of CrossWeb EX financial software.

items.title: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to backdoor WordPress sites
items.summary: A threat actor breached TeamUpdraft, compromising UpdraftCentral connection keys that can issue commands to connected WordPress sites.

items.title: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates
items.summary: Mozilla, Google, Apple, and others blocked eight eMudhra intermediate certificates after weak private keys were exposed, preventing forged trusted certificates.

items.title: AI raised the floor. The hacker crowd keeps raising the ceiling.
items.summary: Intigriti data shows AI raises the baseline for vulnerability discovery, but human bug bounty remains essential; researchers use multi‑agent workflows and CrowdRecon demonstrates extensive hacker reconnaissance coverage.

items.title: Philippines-based American pleads guilty to running expansive fraud scheme targeting US servicemembers
items.summary: Robert Wayne Boling Jr. pleaded guilty to an identity‑theft conspiracy targeting thousands of U.S. military members and veterans; he faces up to 40 years in prison.

items.title: Indian certification authority eMudhra’s private keys compromised – one of them was the number ‘4’
items.summary: eMudhra’s private keys were compromised, enabling impersonation of any website or service; a large cleanup effort is underway.

items.title: Auto tech startup claims it traced hack attempt back to rival's IP address
items.summary: IQ.Lvbs claims it traced a hack attempt back to rival Comma.ai’s IP address, suggesting unfair competition.

items.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
items.summary: Google, Mozilla, Apple, the Go project, and others blocked eMudhra certificates linked to eight compromised keys; the compromise source remains unclear.

items.title: Bullhorn sees red after cyberattack knocks recruitment platform offline
items.summary: Staffing software giant calls in CrowdStrike as customers face login headaches and questions remain over possible data theft

items.title: AI Agent Adoption Creates Risk as Oversight Struggles to Keep Pace, Splunk Finds
items.summary: Rapid adoption of agentic AI comes with potential business benefits. But if done incorrectly it also carries risks around AI activity management and security

items.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
items.summary: WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's…
